tells: A specific, witty idea: each credit is designed as a period cigarette pack, which fits a film about a tobacco lobbyist

Typography with a point of view: every pack has its own vernacular lettering (script, Clarendon-style serif, condensed sans, art deco), and the gags land ('David Koechner LIGHTS', 'Honey-toasted tobacco lights')
A rich, deliberate retro palette that changes per pack (navy and gold, orange and cream, red, white and blue, mint)
Printed-ephemera texture and halftone-style illustration (hound, airplane, eagle) that look researched, not clip-art
Ends on the row of filters, a visual punchline that closes the sequence
gaps: Mostly flat pan-and-slide across pack surfaces; it needs B's dimensional camera and mechanical choreography
Light is flat print scans with little depth or atmosphere
The structure is repetitive (one pack per credit); B escalates to a climactic reveal and this does less of that

tells: Each frame is a different world: a fleshy translucent hand pulling a coral-red organic heart over a rust-lit mountain ridge, a monochrome volcanic landscape erupting a pink plume, a glass-and-amber organism against a sky gradient, a woven fabric and fibre biome, and glossy olive tubes looped through frosted rings around a red berry cluster
Material work is complex and deliberate: subsurface scattering on skin, mesh netting, frayed fibres, refractive glass, metallic olive lacquer. This is not stock 3D primitives
The palette is unusual and controlled (dusty rose, sage, amber, pale cyan, bottle green) and it shifts across scenes while the frames still read as one family
Small studio/collaborator name tags (Boldtron, Medusa Lab, OFFF MX) suggest a festival opener or collective title sequence, which is a real context for this kind of work
The frames show escalation and transformation from organic to synthetic to dense tangle, which points to choreography rather than a looped effect
gaps: The typography is just functional name tags in a bold grotesk and does nothing for the image. B integrates the credits into the world of the piece, and A should do the same with its type
There is no single unifying narrative thread. It reads as a showcase of beautiful vignettes, not one idea built only for this film, as B's mechanical map is
The surreal-organic-CGI vocabulary is close to the current festival-opener house style. It needs a more personal twist to stand out from its peers

tells: The idea belongs to this piece alone: the world map becomes a clockwork pop-up model, so the geography and politics of the story are literally built in front of you each episode
There is real material storytelling in engraved bronze astrolabe bands, carved wood and brass mechanisms, aged parchment and verdigris tones
The light is motivated: the sun inside the armillary sphere flares through the opening and closing bands, bookending the sequence
The credits are set in a carefully chosen spaced classical serif with a small house-sigil bullet, placed in the space each camera move opens up
The choreography is obvious across frames: a sphere reveal, a tracking flyover of rising cities, a macro mechanism, the map with the pin, and the logo lockup that closes it
gaps: The middle palette leans a little on desaturated grey-green and is murky next to the golden bookends
The credit type is small and sometimes fights with busy detail (for example over the Winterfell mechanism)
The logo lockup is the most conventional frame in the piece, with a heraldic emblem on a glow, and could match the ingenuity of the map

tells: The concept is sharp and specific to the film: every credit is a mid-century cigarette pack, which makes the satire's subject the design language of the titles

The typography has range and a point of view. It reproduces period packaging lettering (arched banner script, Clarendon-style serifs, deco caps, brush script) and fits each name to its own fictional brand
Each fictional brand has its own palette (royal blue and gold, orange and cream, red-white-blue Americana, menthol green), all faithful to printed-ephemera inks
The texture of real print stock is there: halftone, registration, aged paper, engraved illustrations (bloodhound, eagle, airplane, palm fronds)
Wry detail rewards attention: 'Lights' under an actor's name, 'Underage sale prohibited', and a closing row of cigarette filters under the director credit
gaps: The motion is restrained, mostly cuts and pans across flat artwork, so the piece lacks the spatial choreography and weight of B
The structure repeats as pack after pack. The device works, but the frames show no escalation or turn in the final act
The light is flat scanned-print light by design, with no depth or atmosphere. That fits the concept but limits the film's visual range

defects: Faint lighter rectangular panel visible behind the lower-left area (edge near x≈210 in frames 4–6 and pairs rows 2–3): a background or compositing seam that breaks the flat paper field
Final ~1s is fully static (change 0.1/s), so the film ends in dead air with no settle beat

The '04' weight/width interpolation reads as a linear variable-font tween; there is no anticipation, overshoot or settle, and the glyph's lower-left terminal shows a notch where the morph happens mid-tween
Headline is simply present in frame 2 and body/footer arrive by opacity fade only; the elements don't hand off to each other
The red vertical rule stays inert for the whole piece and is never activated as a grid device
Footer arrives late as a low-contrast fade that is still mid-opacity in pairs row 1
gaps: Choreography: one move (a variable-axis morph from heavy condensed to light extended on '04') plus opacity fades. There is no staggered layout build, no grid reveal and no spatial motion to make 'form follows the grid' visible, so the claimed idea goes unshown

Timing and arc: the energy front-loads in seconds 1–3 and then flatlines, with no peak at 60–80% and no release or rhyming end state. The morph needs eased curves with weight (slow-in, fast middle, soft settle) and a final accent beat

Finish and material: the flat digital paper has no texture, grain or light, and a visible panel seam sits behind the lower-left. It is clean, but it reads as a web-page screenshot rather than a crafted frame
